title: Present perfect progressive: I have been writing

blocks.text: As it can be seen from the above explanations English tenses may be rendered in Russian by either the imperfective or the perfective aspect of the corresponding Russian verbs. However, the following hints may be helpful:

head: English
Russian
rows: 2. Present Perfect Progressive: I have been writing all morning.
Present, imperfective: Я пишу уже всё утро. («уже» usually added)
3. Any progressive tense: I am writing a letter. I was writing a letter. I will be writing a letter.
Imperfective aspect of the corresponding verb: Я пишу письмо. Я писал письмо. Я буду писать письмо.

blocks.text: Also present perfect if it means that the action continues through the present: *I have lived here for one year already.* — **Я живу здесь уже год.**

items: Дождь идет со вторника.
It has been raining since Tuesday.
Мы живём здесь с июля.
We've been living here since July.
Я целую ночь тут сижу.
I've been sitting here all night.
Я уже целую вечность жду.
I've been waiting forever.
Они работают над новой вакциной.
They've been working on a new vaccine.
Том ведёт себя как детсадовец.
Tom has been behaving like a kindergarten kid.
Жак уже два года занимается дзюдо.
Jacques has been doing judo for two years.
Я учу русский с ноября.
I have been learning Russian since November.
Цены неуклонно растут.
Prices have been rising steadily.
Моя дочь уже четыре года страдает анорексией.
My daughter has been suffering from anorexia for four years already.
